subject: Urban Planning
subcategory: Parks, Green Spaces, and Public Land
title: Cheonggyecheon: Burying a Highway, Finding a River
description: A quick, practical guide to Cheonggyecheon: Burying a Highway, Finding a River.

hook.text: Seoul tore down an elevated highway and uncovered the stream it had buried. The result is beautiful.

buildup.text: The Cheonggyecheon stream was covered with concrete in the 1960s, then an expressway was built on top.

discovery.text: In 2003, the city demolished the highway and restored the stream with walkways, bridges, and greenery.

twist.text: Temperatures along the stream dropped 3.6°C compared to surrounding streets. Nature cooled the city.

climax.text: The project cost $900 million but generated billions in economic activity and revived a dead neighborhood.

punchline.text: They removed a highway and found a river. The city came alive.

quiz.question: What environmental effect did restoring the Cheonggyecheon stream produce?
options: Air pollution increased due to slower traffic on surrounding roads
Temperatures along the stream dropped 3.6°C compared to nearby streets
Flooding risk increased because the stream couldn't handle storm water
